routes.label: at the constituency's Registration Unit: two to three weeks

note: Antigua and Barbuda's identity card is the Electoral Commission's electoral identification card, to which every registered elector (18 or over) is entitled; ABEC calls it one of the preferred forms of national identification. It is valid ten years, and under the Registration Regulations an expired card is replaced free by the Registration Officer of the constituency, in two to three weeks. A lost card costs EC$100 (pensioners and holders of a police or fire report exempt, not modelled); a separate fee for a first card isn't stated, so the free renewal is the offer.

sources.title: Antigua and Barbuda Electoral Commission, Electoral Identification Card
sources.said: All of these individuals are entitled to a state of the art electoral identification card that is produced at ABEC. The ID card is one of the preferred forms of national identification and it is widely accepted in both the private and public sectors. It is valid for ten years ... "On the expiration of an identification card an elector shall apply to the Registration Officer for the constituency in which he resides for a replacement free of charge".

sources.title: Antigua and Barbuda Electoral Commission, Frequently asked questions
sources.said: How long will it take to replace the Expired Voter’s ID card? The process should take two -three weeks. Is there a fee to replace the Expired Voter’s ID Card? There is no fee to replace expired card. ... The electoral identification card is valid for ten years. ... The cost of a replacement card is ... $100 EC
